stories.title: People really hate AI, so why can’t they get enough?
stories.excerpt: Over the summer I talked to the CEO of Springboards, a startup building an LLM that’s designed to come up with a wider variety of responses than its mainstream rivals do. At the start of the call, he said something that’s been stuck in my head since: “We often say that we’re a self-loathing AI…
stories.lead: “I guess that makes me a self-loathing AI journalist,” I replied. It was a joke! I love my job. But I do not love many of the things the technology I write about has become: warped by hype, steered by zealots, inescapable.

stories.title: Strings and Character Data in Python
stories.excerpt: Work with Python strings using a rich set of operators and functions: string literals, the str() function, and the methods you'll use most.
stories.lead:
Python strings are a sequence of characters used for handling textual data. You can create strings in Python using quotation marks or the str() function, which converts objects into strings. Strings in Python are immutable, meaning once you define a string, you can’t change it.

By the end of this tutorial, you’ll understand that:

You’ll explore creating strings with string literals and functions, using operators and built-in functions with strings, indexing and slicing techniques, and methods for string interpolation and formatting. These skills will help you manipulate and format textual data in your Python programs effectively.

stories.title: Quiz: Python's collections: A Buffet of Specialized Data Types
stories.excerpt: Check your understanding of Python's collections module and the specialized container data types it provides, from namedtuple to ChainMap.
stories.lead:
In this quiz, you’ll test your understanding of Python’s collections: A Buffet of Specialized Data Types.

Python’s collections module provides specialized container data types that approach specific programming problems more clearly and more efficiently than the general purpose built-ins do.

You’ll revisit namedtuple() for readable code, deque for queues and stacks, defaultdict for missing keys, OrderedDict for ordering, Counter for tallies, ChainMap for multiple mappings, and the wrapper classes for customizing built-ins.

stories.title: Nobel Prize awarded for showing how nerve cells shape feelings
stories.excerpt: US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and his German colleagues Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel have been awarded for their work.
stories.lead:
Per Svenningsson, chair of the Nobel Committee for Physiology or Medicine, explained: "Optogenetics provides opportunities for mapping the brain in a way that we could once only dream of."

Before, the inner workings behind feelings, behaviours and bodily functions were more of a mystery to scientists.

Optogentics is a way to illuminate brain pathways, using a special protein borrowed from algae that scientists use to control cell electrical activity using light.

stories.title: US air force removes all bombers from British military base RAF Fairford
stories.excerpt: No reason has been given for the withdrawal, but it follows a major incident last week when police were alerted to "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase.
stories.lead:
The US has withdrawn all of its bombers from RAF Fairford, the UK military base at the centre of an incident being investigated by counter-terror police.

A statement from a Pentagon official confirmed on Sunday it had removed its bombers - thought to be about a dozen B-1s - from the base back to their home stations in America.

US media reported a new threat led to the bombers being removed, which follows a major incident on 27 September when police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase.

stories.title: Nobel Prize in medicine awarded to trio for optogenetics work

stories.title: Voters are increasingly using AI chatbots to fact-check and compare candidates
stories.excerpt: Voters are already voting in the midterms. This year, some voters are trying something new to get ready for the election: asking AI to help research their ballot and even decide who to vote for.
stories.lead:
Stay up to date with our Politics newsletter, sent weekly.

On a September evening, Adam Johnson, 40, settled on his porch chair in Morgantown, West Virginia, to go over his ballot for the upcoming midterm election.

Chatting through all the races and the different candidates, he worked to figure out who best represented his values. But rather than discussing it with a friend or family member, he held an hours-long discussion with ChatGPT — a chatbot powered by a large language model (LLM) owned by OpenAI, an AI research company.

stories.title: Shadow chancellor to unveil Tory plans to cut taxes and regulations
stories.excerpt: Shadow ministers will unveil a series of policies on day two of the Conservative Party conference in Birmingham.
stories.lead:
Conservative shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith is to outline his plans for the UK economy, including hopes to cut taxes, red tape and house-building costs.

Griffith and his colleagues will also use day two of the party's conference in Birmingham to explain how they would want to reduce food costs, support Heathrow Airport expansion, and abolish Natural England and the Environment Agency.

Another prospective policy is replacing agreements designed to compel developers to fund community projects and services in areas they want to build.

stories.title: Supreme Court's new term kicks off with blockbuster climate change case
stories.excerpt: The case centers on whether local governments can hold giant energy companies accountable for the local harms of climate change, but it has repercussions beyond climate.
stories.lead:
A new Supreme Court term begins Monday with arguments in a blockbuster case about the reach of state power.

Boulder, Colo., is suing two big energy companies, arguing they deceived people about the harms of fossil fuels and contributed to disasters that cost Boulder a lot of time and money.

The dispute could have ramifications far beyond the climate, to other areas where states are trying to hold companies accountable for their alleged harms to local communities.

stories.title: Harvard Men's Water Polo Picks Up Pair of Wins
stories.excerpt: Crimson take down LIU and Iona on the road in conference play.
stories.lead:
BROOKLYN, N.Y. -- The Harvard men's water polo picked up its first NWPC win of the season with an 18-14 victory at LIU on Sunday morning and finished the day with a pair of wins after defeating Iona, 18-7, in New Rochelle.

Harvard is 5-10 overall and 2-1 in the NWPC. The Crimson never trailed LIU (6-9, 1-3) and led 10-6 at halftime before needing to withstand several runs by the Sharks in the third and fourth quarters to escape with the win. Dean Strauser and Jack Burghardt each led the Crimson with four goals apiece.
